override.repo_standard: The scripts/verify_*.py convention in this repo: each verifier is a standalone, stdlib-only script that imports no sibling verifier or producer (verify_skip_guard.py and verify_fowler_pass.py both re-declare rather than import). The handoff additionally forbids touching scripts/context_manifest.py.
override.reason: DECLARATION_KEY = "context_refs" is defined in both verify_context_declaration.py and context_manifest.py, and each test module carries its own importlib load() helper. De-duplicating would couple a read-only lint to the producer it lints, which the convention exists to prevent; the duplication is explicitly documented at verify_context_declaration.py:36-38. The standard subordinates the smell.

override.repo_standard: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's new Task-table row plus scripts/context_manifest.py:59-63 define {root, path, required} as the declared on-disk schema of a context_refs entry.
override.reason: The triple travels together because it IS the published JSON schema, not an accidental grouping. Introducing a value object in a lint that reads raw JSON would add a mapping layer between the file and the check it performs. Documented schema wins.

smells.finding: The declared filesystem path is treated as a bare string and tested against the prose with plain substring containment (verify_context_declaration.py:76, `if path not in prose`). Modelling a path as an untyped substring is what produces blocker B2: a declared `agents/GLOSSARY.md` passes clean when the prose names `docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md`, because one is a substring of the other, even though the two name different files. Minimal fix keeps the string but adds a delimiter-boundary test (start-of-string / whitespace / quote / backtick / paren before the match) rather than raw `in`.

The lint's direction statement is triplicated verbatim-ish across three files: the module docstring (verify_context_declaration.py:17-26), the new committed narrative in docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md, and the fixture `_readme` in tests/fixtures/context_declaration_lint.json. Correcting the inverted claim (blocker B1) therefore requires three coordinated edits, and the same wording being wrong in all three is direct evidence of the cost. Low severity for a corpus this size, but it is why B1 shipped past self-review.

override.repo_standard: The scripts/verify_*.py CLI convention: a no-args default that discovers the real corpus, plus an explicit path list that bypasses discovery (matching verify_skip_guard.py's positional-report shape).
override.reason: The `--root` flag and discover_templates() exist only for the not-yet-wired CI invocation, which would otherwise read as speculative. But both paths are exercised by DiscoveryTests and CliTests, the CI wiring is a named follow-up the implementer already raised as a triage candidate, and the convention requires the no-args form. Sanctioned, not speculative.

smells.finding: Not deodorant in the classic sense (the code is clear), but a stronger form of the same failure: the module docstring at verify_context_declaration.py:17-20 describes behaviour the code does not have, asserting the lint catches 'a path quietly dropped from context_refs while the prose still implies it is read' when that case provably exits 0. A comment that misdescribes its own function is worse than one that compensates for it, because it is what a future maintainer will trust. This is blocker B1.
